title: Inherited Multisig Wallets: '2 of 3' Setups and the Descriptor File
plain:
A wallet marked '2 of 3' is a shared-control setup: three hardware wallets were created together, and any two of the three devices can move the funds. Two devices are enough to act — the third is a spare that adds safety, not a requirement to get started. But the descriptor file is needed too — it describes the whole setup, including which devices belong together and how many signatures are required. Keep all three devices and the file together, so that a single future loss never leaves you with fewer than two working devices.

The envelope labeled 'descriptor' that looks like computer code is valuable — do not clean it up or throw it away. The descriptor is not a secret by itself: it is a description of how the wallet was built, not a key. But it is required to rebuild a multisig wallet, so without it, even two working devices cannot show you the coins. Keep it with the key locations and list it in the inventory so it never gets mistaken for junk.

If one of the three hardware wallets is missing, the coins are not lost. No — two of three still works, so with any two devices plus the descriptor you can recover the funds. Do not panic, and do not reset or wipe the devices you still have. Check the backup locations first and keep searching for the third — it may turn up in a safe deposit box, another room, or with someone the owner trusted.

Can you open the wallet right now with just the two devices and the descriptor? Yes — a 2-of-3 setup opens with any two devices plus the descriptor. But still do the full Day 6 verification sequence first: clean computer, verified software, then the devices. One difficult thing per day — do not rush the first real action. Viewing the balance does not move the coins; sending them is a separate step for later, after everything checks out.

Two rules never change, no matter how confident you feel: never type seed words into a computer, website, or app, and never reset or wipe any device before every backup is verified. If anyone pressures you to move the coins quickly, stop and slow down — that pressure itself is a common scam warning sign.
technical:
A '2 of 3' label denotes a threshold-signature policy: three cosigning keys were generated, and a valid spend requires any two signatures. Any two of the three devices can move the funds; the third exists for redundancy. The descriptor (an output descriptor or wallet-configuration file listing the script type, the three extended public keys, and derivation paths) is mandatory recovery metadata: wallet software cannot reconstruct the multisig addresses from the devices alone, so the descriptor file is needed too — it describes the whole setup. The descriptor contains no private keys and cannot move funds by itself, but it reveals the wallet's existence and balance to whoever holds it, so store it with the same care as other inheritance documents and list it in the inventory.

Recovery procedure: on a clean, dedicated computer, obtain wallet software from its official source and verify it, then connect any two of the three devices and load the wallet from the descriptor. If one device is missing, the setup remains fully recoverable — two of three still works — but keep searching for the third and do not reset or wipe any device before backup verification is complete. Never type any cosigner's seed words into the computer; the devices sign directly. Balance viewing is read-only, and the first spend requires on-device confirmation on both devices, so pace it: one difficult thing per day.

warnings: Never type seed words into any computer, phone, website, or app — the devices sign directly and the words stay offline.
Never reset or wipe a hardware wallet before every backup and recovery document has been verified.

The descriptor is not a private key, but avoid sharing it publicly: it reveals the wallet's existence and balance to whoever holds it.
